claims.text: In single-phase high-entropy alloys, atomic-size-mismatch-induced lattice distortion is the primary mechanism governing hardness.
In single-phase high-entropy alloys, atomic-size-mismatch-induced lattice distortion is the primary mechanism governing strength.
A larger average atomic size mismatch increases local lattice distortion.
Greater local lattice distortion creates stronger barriers to dislocation motion.
Stronger barriers to dislocation motion enhance hardness.
Stronger barriers to dislocation motion enhance yield strength.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening can be used to quantify the degree of lattice distortion.
An HEA with higher atomic size mismatch will exhibit greater lattice distortion than a lower-mismatch baseline.
An HEA with higher atomic size mismatch will exhibit significantly higher hardness than a lower-mismatch baseline within the single-phase regime.
An HEA with higher atomic size mismatch will exhibit significantly higher yield strength than a lower-mismatch baseline within the single-phase regime.
Grain-size variations can independently influence mechanical properties through grain-boundary strengthening.
Secondary-phase formation can independently influence mechanical properties.
The proposed mismatch–distortion–strength relationship is limited to homogeneous, single-phase HEAs at ambient temperature without significant confounding microstructural changes.
Electronic-structure effects or short-range ordering may interact with the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism.
